outcome: Warmup reuse is real, but the approved input model does not establish the normal-pressure opportunity under native ownership. Prefix readiness is not free-LRU entry. A native control retaining the original request through its prior observed completion removes the fixed-versus-queue BG contrast in both seeds. No arbitrary admission policy was added.

input_contract.note: Only the approved normal-pressure gate was exercised. Stress remains a control, not an added required contrast gate. Runner-only paper/question/arrival fields never entered a value policy.

warmup.observation_source: Existing ActualAdoption/scheduled-range ledger, not get_cached_blocks or queued-provider probe frequency.

native_free_order.meaning: Native free releases the trailing end before the leading prefix. Lost trailing blocks leave a usable leading prefix; there is no binary whole-prefix loss in these early-release cases.

duplicate_hash_control.meaning: A physical eviction alone is not evidence of lost logical reuse while another cached copy exists. This availability probe was not used as a reuse/value label.

preflight_ready.interpretation: The optimistic preflight-release geometry has a partial-prefix contrast, not the assumed full837-block loss.

prior_original_completion.interpretation: Keeping the original native owner through the supplied prior completion observation leaves no normal-pressure BG opportunity at the frozen third-request arrivals, even when the warmup owner is released at the optimistic ready boundary.

leading_prefix_counterfactual.label: leading75_counterfactual; not a policy
leading_prefix_counterfactual.interpretation: Prefix-closed partial FG retention is natively valid and meets the actual matched75% token gate. This particular counterfactual sacrifices more FG savings than the BG work it restores. It is neither an admission event nor proof that every other allocation has the same net value.

native_findings.legacy_owners: All12 cases restored the native pool and kept historical retained_block_seconds=0. No retention owner was introduced.

gate_interpretation: The model's warmup-ready timestamp cannot be used as the prefix's FREE-LRU aging origin while another request still holds it.
The normal-pressure opportunity is sensitive to this native ownership boundary and is not established by the supplied input/cache model.

The prior-completion control uses an observation from a previous run, not measured lifetimes from the new424-request execution. This is a concrete native counterexample to the preflight inference, not proof that every future GPU execution must lack contrast.
Other BG requests complete immediately in this controlled native replay; actual concurrent allocator churn and decode traffic remain unmeasured for the424 probe.
FG comparisons cover the first reuse wave, where the model's matched savings occur. They are native token results, not a full424-request GPU performance or quality claim.
The original0/4 full-parent zero-own-benefit floor remains separate from displaced BG cost and net marginal value. Positive FG own savings were not relabeled as zero.

implementation_not_started.reason: The user required this native gate before arbitrary policy work. Confirm the actual last-owner release and effective native eviction opportunity before selecting a value rule.

raw_native_evidence.fields: duplicate_hash_probe; cases[] with warmup ActualAdoption, shared-reference/free state, exact native prefix free-depth order, test leading hit/resident/missing/evicted-depth evidence, matched FG recompute, no-lease count and final pool restoration; comparisons[] with actual FG savings fraction and BG recompute deltas.

derived_native_gate.fields: policy_ready=false; native_cases; gate; native_free_order; comparisons[] plus FG savings sacrificed and net recompute reduction; explicit limitations.

stable_exports.not_a_policy_schema: These exports are native feasibility evidence only. They do not stand in for future prospective admission/exposure/ranking evidence.
